topic: Project history and dormancy basis (Port Sudan / Red Sea LNG import terminal)
wiki_text: Sunagas (state-linked, Khartoum) signed a lease with the Sudan Ports Authority in July 2018 for Sudan's first LNG import terminal at Port Sudan on the Red Sea, with Sofregaz (France) providing front-end engineering and design. The plan centered on an FSRU (~6.17 mtpa, ~US$500 million) to fast-track gas supply to a planned Port Sudan power station, ahead of a larger onshore terminal. Sunagas issued EPC/FSRU tender documentation in 2018 (for a 125,000-175,000 cbm FSRU, max ~750 MMscf/d) and received two bids — from Qatar Petroleum and from Trafigura partnered with Dreifa Energy. No contract award, FID, or construction was subsequently reported; the project has shown no public progress since ~2018-2019. Sudan's civil war (from April 2023) has further frozen Port Sudan infrastructure. GEM therefore records the terminal as inferred shelved (2024) and inferred cancelled (2026) under the dormancy rules.
